newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Gruntal raises ValuJet.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Gruntal raises ValuJet.

text.p: Gruntal & Co analyst Steve Lewins raised his rating on ValuJet Inc to neutral from underperform on Thursday, saying he expects the grounded discount carrier to get final government approval to resume service soon.
Lewins said in a report to investors that ValuJet shares provide a trading opportunity for highly aggressive accounts.
The stock later was up 2-1/4 at 12-1/2 in active trading on the Nasdaq market.
"ValuJet may be in the air within a week," said Lewin, noting that the carrier has waited longer than expectedl for a fitness order from the U.S. Department of Transportation.

As to what can be expected in terms of the company's operations, the analyst added: "There are no fundamentals with which to work, except unit costs probably will be hefty when the airline returns to the skies -- perhaps in the eight-cent per available seat mile range."
He also made several points for investors to take into consideration, including:

** despite reports that ValuJet will sell $75 million of aircraft at cost to pay down $162.5 million, he expects the carrier to make gains on many of its planes and devote only $55-60 million to debt payments with the rest going to complete upgrade and improvement work on two DC-9s;
** McDonnell Douglas Corp, shy on older DC-9s for its own customers, may be the key negotiator to purchase 12-14 DC-9s and MD-80s from ValuJet;
** ValuJet had cash on hand of $208 million at the end of the second quarter and probably will end the quarter with more than $150 million;
** initial unit costs will be hefty and promotional pricing will keep the revenue yield low once flights resume, so near-term losses are likely;

** ValuJet would return to the skies under strict regulatory supervision, at a time when Delta Air Lines Inc will compete with its new low-cost Delta Express operation and Southwest Airlines Co is increasing its presence in Florida and at other points east of the Mississippi.
